chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said:
"If a man were to die while fasting during travel, I would not perform the funeral prayer for him."

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state in which the ruling applies
key_terms.الصَّادِقِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the transmitter of the ruling
key_terms.رَجُلًا: a man; the hypothetical subject mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.صَلَّيْتُ: I would perform prayer; here referring to the funeral prayer
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ: for him; over the deceased person
key_terms.مَاتَ: died; indicating the case reaching death while in that state

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about someone who fasts while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys the legal severity of fasting while traveling when the ruling requires that the fast be shortened or not observed in that state. The statement emphasizes that such fasting is contrary to the prescribed law and underscores the importance of complying with the divinely ordained rulings of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1975 - Muhammad ibn Hakim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that he said:
"If a man were to die while fasting during travel, I would not perform the funeral prayer for him."
